question: With herdr-run restoring egress, can the landing cascade execute -- starting with 'push the parent'?
answer: No. git egress works and gh does not; parent main has diverged 118/40 with 9 two-sided conflicts in the ci-hub landing gate; and Stacks 1/2/4 have no landable artifact because the plan that names them explicitly wrote no code and opened no PR.

egress.gh: BROKEN -- api.github.com 'network is unreachable' even under with-proxy; no gh pr merge is possible
egress.herdr_run_bug: bare 'gh <subcommand>' is refused: the allowlist reads the second token as the program unless a with-proxy prefix is present

method: git merge-tree --write-tree (non-destructive; the parent working tree is dirty with other agents' work and was never touched). Per-file classification uses whitespace-insensitive numstat against the explicit merge-base and explicit remote-main SHA, not FETCH_HEAD.
limitations: Conflict classification is by diff shape, not by reading every hunk. 'TWO-SIDED-needs-adjudication' means both sides changed the file substantially from the base; it does not prejudge which side is right.
The 40 remote commits are codex-coord's work; their intent was not available to this fleet.
Nothing was landed and no stack was tagged implemented.
